title: 108. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Scaling Recipes and Mixtures
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Scaling a Recipe Using Direct Proportion
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the amount of an ingredient needed when a recipe is scaled up.
questions.question: A recipe for \(4\) servings uses \(200\text{ g}\) of flour. How much flour is needed for \(6\) servings at the same rate? Round to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The flour amount scales by \(\frac{6}{4}\): \(200\times\frac{6}{4}=300.00\text{ g}\). The alternative reverses the scale factor: \(200\times\frac{4}{6}\approx 133.33\text{ g}\).
questions.hint: Compare the target number of servings with the original number of servings.

questions.concept: Scaling a Recipe Using Direct Proportion
questions.learningObjective: Calculate the amount of rice needed when a recipe is scaled up.
questions.question: A recipe for \(3\) people uses \(150\text{ g}\) of rice. How much rice is needed for \(5\) people at the same rate?
questions.explanation: The rice amount is \(150\times\frac{5}{3}=250\text{ g}\). The alternative reverses the scale factor: \(150\times\frac{3}{5}=90\text{ g}\).
questions.hint: Compare the target batch size with the original batch size.

questions.concept: Scaling a Mixture Using a Ratio
questions.learningObjective: Determine an unknown quantity in a mixture using a given ratio.
questions.question: A juice mixture uses juice and water in the ratio \(2:5\). If \(4\text{ L}\) of juice is used, how much water is needed?
questions.explanation: Each juice part corresponds to \(\frac{5}{2}\) water parts, so the water is \(4\times\frac{5}{2}=10\text{ L}\). The alternative uses the juice-to-water ratio in the wrong direction: \(4\times\frac{2}{5}=1.6\text{ L}\).
questions.hint: Keep the stated order of the two mixture components.

questions.concept: Scaling a Recipe Using Direct Proportion
questions.learningObjective: Determine the amount of flour needed when a recipe is scaled up.
questions.question: A recipe uses \(2\text{ cups}\) of flour to make \(12\) cookies. How many cups of flour are needed to make \(30\) cookies at the same rate?
questions.explanation: The flour amount is \(2\times\frac{30}{12}=5\text{ cups}\). The alternative reverses the scale factor: \(2\times\frac{12}{30}=0.8\text{ cups}\).
questions.hint: Compare the target number of cookies with the original number of cookies.

questions.concept: Scaling a Mixture Using a Ratio
questions.learningObjective: Determine an unknown quantity in a paint mixture using a given ratio.
questions.question: A paint mixture uses paint and thinner in the ratio \(3:4\). If \(12\text{ L}\) of paint is used, how much thinner is needed?
questions.explanation: The thinner amount is \(12\times\frac{4}{3}=16\text{ L}\). The alternative reverses the component ratio: \(12\times\frac{3}{4}=9\text{ L}\).
questions.hint: Keep the stated order of the two mixture components.

questions.concept: Scaling a Recipe Using Direct Proportion
questions.learningObjective: Determine the amount of milk needed when a recipe is scaled up.
questions.question: A recipe for \(8\) servings uses \(500\text{ mL}\) of milk. How much milk is needed for \(12\) servings at the same rate? Round to two decimal places.
questions.explanation: The milk amount is \(500\times\frac{12}{8}=750.00\text{ mL}\). The alternative reverses the scale factor: \(500\times\frac{8}{12}\approx 333.33\text{ mL}\).
questions.hint: Compare the target batch size with the original batch size.

questions.concept: Scaling a Mixture Using a Ratio
questions.learningObjective: Determine an unknown quantity in a cement mixture using a given ratio.
questions.question: A cement mixture uses cement and sand in the ratio \(1:3\). If \(9\text{ kg}\) of sand is used, how much cement is needed?
questions.explanation: The cement-to-sand ratio is \(1:3\), so the cement mass is \(\frac{9}{3}=3\text{ kg}\). The alternative multiplies the sand mass by \(3\), \(9\times 3=27\), instead of dividing to recover one part of cement.
questions.hint: Identify the ingredient or mixture component actually requested.

questions.concept: Scaling a Recipe Using Direct Proportion
questions.learningObjective: Determine the amount of pasta needed when a recipe is scaled up.
questions.question: A recipe for \(5\) people uses \(200\text{ g}\) of pasta. How much pasta is needed for \(8\) people at the same rate?
questions.explanation: The pasta amount is \(200\times\frac{8}{5}=320\text{ g}\). The alternative reverses the scale factor: \(200\times\frac{5}{8}=125\text{ g}\).
questions.hint: Compare the target batch size with the original batch size.

questions.concept: Scaling a Mixture Using a Ratio
questions.learningObjective: Determine an unknown quantity in a salad dressing mixture using a given ratio.
questions.question: A salad dressing uses oil and vinegar in the ratio \(5:2\). If \(15\text{ mL}\) of oil is used, how much vinegar is needed?
questions.explanation: The vinegar amount is \(15\times\frac{2}{5}=6\text{ mL}\). The alternative reverses the component ratio: \(15\times\frac{5}{2}=37.5\text{ mL}\).
questions.hint: Keep the stated order of the two mixture components.

questions.concept: Scaling a Recipe Using Direct Proportion
questions.learningObjective: Determine the amount of milk needed when a recipe is scaled up.
questions.question: A recipe for \(4\) servings uses \(250\text{ mL}\) of cream and \(300\text{ mL}\) of milk. How much milk is needed for \(10\) servings at the same rate?
questions.explanation: Use the original milk amount, giving \(300\times\frac{10}{4}=750\text{ mL}\). The alternative scales the cream quantity instead of the requested milk quantity: \(250\times\frac{10}{4}=625\text{ mL}\).
questions.hint: Identify the ingredient or mixture component actually requested.
